name: Skin fasting

card.summary: A routine of pausing skincare products or face washing for a period, which followers say lets the skin rebalance and look clearer and less irritated.
card.note: Individual responses vary; those with active skin conditions may see them worsen.

quick.overview:
Skin fasting means stopping most or all skincare products, and sometimes face washing, for days or weeks. Followers say it lets the skin barrier recover, reduces irritation from layered products and gives a more even, natural look.

No published trials of skin fasting as a regimen were found. Dermatology material on related topics notes that barrier damage can come from excessive exfoliation and that moisturising may support the barrier.
quick.how: People typically cut back to the basics or nothing for a set period, then reintroduce products one at a time to see which suit them. Duration and strictness vary between people.
quick.risks: Skipping cleansing or sunscreen may leave dirt, oil or sun exposure unaddressed, and people with acne or dry skin may notice flare-ups. Dermatology sources describe gentle washing and moisturising for dry skin.

lead: Skin fasting, also called skin detox, is a routine in which a person pauses skincare products or washing for a time. The aim is a calmer, clearer complexion by reducing the number of products and irritants in contact with the face.

Proponents say the skin can regulate itself once the load of products is removed. Dermatology references on skin care discuss related points: excessive exfoliation can damage the barrier, moisturising twice a day may strengthen it, and overwashing may cause dryness but is not described as causing oil overproduction [1].

angle.text: Followers use the break to reduce irritation and redness, hoping the skin looks clearer and more balanced afterward.

paras: The practice ranges from dropping a few active products to using only water. People often reintroduce products gradually afterward.

Wikipedia's skin care article describes barrier damage from excess exfoliation, barrier benefits of moisturising, and says overwashing does not cause sebum overproduction but may cause dryness [1]. Skin fasting as a regimen is not addressed there.
